title: UK Labour Market Nowcast

staff.underlying_text: Underlying employment growth has also softened recently.
Bank staff judge that underlying employment growth, based on the signal from a range of measures, has been around zero since the end of last year.
A range of indicators suggests that underlying employment growth remains close to zero.
Underlying employment growth has been around zero over the past year.

unemployment.text: The unemployment rate is expected to rise further to 5.3% by mid-2026.

unemployment.text: Bank staff project the unemployment rate to rise to 5.1% in 2026 Q2.

unemployment.text: Bank staff project the unemployment rate to rise gradually to 5.0% in 2026 Q3 and 5.1% in Q4.
Bank staff project the unemployment rate to rise gradually to 5.0% in 2026 Q3 and 5.1% in Q4.

staff_method: Bank staff's indicator-based measure of underlying employment growth is constructed using a dynamic factor model following the approach of Doz et al (2011). The model extracts a common component from monthly survey indicators, capturing comovements across series. The common component is scaled to align with LFS employment growth between 2000-19.
